title: Manila airport pickup: how to find your driver after landing
description: Confirm the airport meeting point, pickup contact and hotel branch before your private transfer in Manila.
summary: Ask for a meeting point you can recognise on foot, a driver contact and a fallback if either phone loses signal. Send the arrival date in Philippine local time, especially on an overnight flight.

sections.heading: Before departure
paragraphs: Give the flight number and the hotel name with its street or district. Two branches of the same hotel can be a long drive apart. Ask the operator to send the confirmed terminal, the meeting instructions and any pickup restrictions together so everyone is working from the same message. Save an offline copy.

sections.heading: If you cannot see the driver
paragraphs: Stay at the agreed spot while you contact dispatch. Describe a visible sign or bay number and ask where to walk before changing levels or crossing to another pickup area. Confirm the driver's name and vehicle details against the dispatch message before boarding.

title: A delayed flight into Manila: how to update a booked transfer
description: Update a booked Manila airport pickup when a flight is delayed, rebooked or moved past midnight.
summary: Tell dispatch as soon as the airline changes your flight. A driver following the original flight number may have no way to connect it to a replacement flight.

sections.heading: A rebooking changes the pickup details
paragraphs: Send the booking reference for your transfer, old and new flight numbers, new arrival date and the airline's latest terminal information. Keep the hotel destination in the message. For a delay past midnight, spell out the date instead of writing “tonight.”

sections.heading: What to confirm before accepting an update
paragraphs: Ask when waiting time starts, how much is included and how the operator handles a missed connection. A flight landing at 21:00 and passengers ready at 22:00 are two different events. Get written confirmation of the revised meeting point, price if changed and the person to contact after landing.

title: Manila van rental with driver: will the luggage fit?
description: Choose a private van for a Manila trip using passenger numbers, bag sizes and the proposed seating layout.
summary: Count people and bags separately. A vehicle advertised for seven occupants can have much less luggage room with every passenger row in use.

sections.heading: Send a luggage manifest
paragraphs: For example, a party of five might carry four checked cases, five small bags and a folded stroller. Give the approximate dimensions of the largest item and say which bags must stay upright. Ask for confirmation against the proposed vehicle with the required seats in place.

sections.heading: Decide on a larger vehicle before pickup
paragraphs: If dispatch suggests folding a seat, check that everyone still has a passenger seat. Ask for a picture of the actual luggage area or its dimensions. For two vehicles, agree which one takes each passenger group and who holds the hotel address if the vehicles get separated.

title: Manila car hire with driver: how to compare overtime charges
description: Compare full-day driver quotes in Manila with a worked overtime example and a checklist of extra charges.
summary: Compare quotes against the same pickup time, final drop-off and route. A cheaper day rate can cost more once the included hours run out.

sections.heading: Price the day you actually need
paragraphs: Suppose an itinerary takes ten hours. An illustrative ₱4,000 offer covering eight hours plus ₱400 per extra hour totals ₱4,800 before extras. A ₱4,600 ten-hour offer is cheaper for that itinerary if other inclusions match. These example figures are for comparison only.

sections.heading: Define the end of the booking
paragraphs: Ask whether the clock starts at your pickup or when the vehicle leaves its base. Check how a partial extra hour is rounded and who authorises an extension. Request separate lines for parking, tolls and out-of-area charges. Give the group leader a copy before the day begins.

title: Booking a Manila driver for a day of business meetings
description: Plan pickups, waiting time and route changes for a Manila business itinerary with several meetings.
summary: Build the booking around the meeting with the least schedule flexibility. Give dispatch actual building entrances, meeting windows and the latest acceptable arrival time.

sections.heading: Use a stop sheet
paragraphs: List the district, building name, visitor entrance and a contact for each stop. Two meetings in the same district can have different vehicle access arrangements. Mark whether the driver should wait nearby or return at a set time. Share route changes with one dispatcher so the driver receives a single version.

sections.heading: Plan for a meeting that runs over
paragraphs: If meeting one ends late, decide in advance which later stop can move. A driver cannot promise a fixed journey time. Agree a message such as “Ready at lobby B in ten minutes” and identify who can approve extra hours. For confidential meetings, give dispatch pickup details without sending the meeting agenda.

title: Planning a private Manila day tour with older travellers
description: Plan a Manila tour around boarding comfort, walking distances, mobility aids and breaks.
summary: Build the day around comfortable boarding, short walks and planned breaks. Ask about the specific passenger's preferences before confirming a vehicle or route.

sections.heading: Start from the passenger's day
paragraphs: Ask how long the group wants to spend between breaks, whether steps are comfortable and how much walking is practical at one stop. For a folding mobility aid, send its folded dimensions. Ask for photos of the proposed vehicle entrance and request confirmation that it can carry both the aid and the group.

sections.heading: Keep the easiest stop optional
paragraphs: Choose one main visit, a meal stop and an optional final visit. Before booking, ask where the driver can legally collect the group and how far that point is from the entrance. If a passenger needs accessible transport or an adapted vehicle, get explicit confirmation of the equipment before paying.

title: How to book a Manila transfer from two or more hotels
description: Coordinate several hotel pickups for one Manila transfer and compare a shared van with separate vehicles.
summary: Send each hotel branch, passenger count and bag count in pickup order. Ask whether a single vehicle can reach the final stop within your time window.

sections.heading: Avoid waiting at the wrong lobby
paragraphs: Send map pins and lobby names rather than hotel brands alone. Make one person at each hotel the pickup contact. If two guests share a large bag, assign it to the stop where it will actually be loaded. A group message should show each party its own ready time.

sections.heading: Compare one van with separate pickups
paragraphs: For a fixed airport departure, ask dispatch to estimate both arrangements. One vehicle can simplify a group booking but adds waiting and loading at each stop. Separate transfers may make sense if the hotels lie on opposite sides of the destination or one party has a different flight.

title: Thuê xe có tài xế ở Manila cho đoàn Việt Nam
description: Mẫu hỏi giá xe riêng ở Manila cho đoàn Việt, từ lịch đón và số vali tới phí chờ và người hỗ trợ.
summary: Gửi DT Tour số người, số vali, ngày giờ theo giờ Philippines và điểm kết thúc chuyến. Nếu cần người hỗ trợ tiếng Việt, hãy ghi rõ bạn cần hỗ trợ qua tin nhắn hay cần người đi cùng đoàn.

sections.heading: Mẫu gửi để nhận báo giá
paragraphs: “Đoàn mình có 6 người lớn, 5 vali lớn. Ngày [ngày] đón tại [khách sạn, chi nhánh], đi [các điểm theo thứ tự], kết thúc tại [địa chỉ] khoảng [giờ]. Nhờ xác nhận loại xe, chỗ hành lý, số giờ và tổng tiền peso.” Nếu đoàn có hai chuyến bay, gửi giờ đến của từng nhóm để bên xe tính phương án đón.

sections.heading: Những khoản cần chốt trước chuyến
paragraphs: Hỏi riêng phí chờ, ngoài giờ, cầu đường, gửi xe và điều kiện đổi lịch. Nếu có một cuộc hẹn bắt buộc, ghi giờ phải có mặt thay vì chỉ ghi giờ xuất phát. Lưu số điều phối, vị trí đón và thông tin xe để cả đoàn vẫn tìm được nhau khi một người mất mạng.

checklist: Báo giá theo lịch của đoàn

title: How to read a Philippine used car's service records
description: Read dates, mileage and completed work on Philippine used-car service records before an inspection.
summary: Make a short timeline from dated job orders. Record the mileage, workshop, work completed and any item deferred on each visit. Use gaps to prepare questions for the seller.

sections.heading: Read the work performed column
paragraphs: A quotation can list work that the owner never approved. Look for a completed job order or receipt and match the vehicle details across documents. If a major part was replaced, ask whether the receipt identifies the part and any applicable warranty. Keep personal addresses and contact details out of shared copies.

sections.heading: Make the timeline useful at inspection
paragraphs: For example, entries at 32,000 and 58,000 kilometres leave a period to explain. The car may have been serviced elsewhere. Ask for the intervening records, then tell your independent inspector which items remain unknown. Missing paperwork alone does not establish neglect.

references.label: DT Car · Used cars in Manila

title: Two offers for your used car in Manila: which pays more?
description: Compare cash offers for a Manila used car after deductions, inspection conditions and payment timing.
summary: Compare the amount payable to you, the deductions still possible and the payment date. A higher preliminary offer may leave you with less at handover.

sections.heading: Put each offer on one line
paragraphs: As an illustration, ₱720,000 less a stated ₱18,000 fee leaves ₱702,000. A direct offer of ₱710,000 with no equivalent fee leaves ₱8,000 more. Before using that comparison, check whether either figure still depends on inspection and whether transport is included.

sections.heading: Agree what can change the figure
paragraphs: Ask the buyer to name unresolved issues and give an expiry date. If a deduction appears after inspection, request the finding and an updated written offer. Retain both versions. Agree who pays any outstanding balance to a lender and when the remainder reaches you, if this applies.

references.label: DT Car · Used cars in Manila

title: Selling a Ford Everest in Manila: details an appraiser needs
description: Prepare your Ford Everest variant, equipment, photos and service details for a Manila appraisal.
summary: Identify the exact year, trim and drivetrain of your Everest before comparing prices. Attach current mileage, service evidence and photos of all seating rows.

sections.heading: Why the trim matters
paragraphs: A buyer searching for one drivetrain or equipment package may skip listings with vague descriptions. Verify the variant from your records and disclose any changes since purchase. Factory equipment, later accessories and missing original parts belong on separate lines. List any spare key and accessories included in the sale.

sections.heading: Use DT Car's Everest photo as a starting point
paragraphs: A photograph of another Everest shows the type of vehicle, but your offer depends on the unit presented. Photograph cargo trim, tailgate, wheels and the seat-folding area alongside exterior views. If your vehicle previously carried equipment, show any mounting marks. Ask for a revised offer after inspection rather than pricing by appearance alone.

references.label: DT Car · Used cars in Manila

title: Viewing a Manila used car when you live outside the city
description: Shortlist a Manila used car remotely with a live walkaround and a confirmed inspection appointment.
summary: Before booking travel, confirm the specific vehicle is available and request a live walkaround. Agree what evidence you need before arranging an independent inspection.

sections.heading: Set the walkaround agenda
paragraphs: Ask the seller to begin outside, walk around the car once, then show the odometer, seat rows, cargo area and any disclosed marks. Ask one or two questions in real time. A recorded advertising clip can help you shortlist but may show the car before a change in condition.

sections.heading: Decide whether the journey is worthwhile
paragraphs: Confirm the inspection venue, available time window and whether the owner can show the service records. Ask what happens if the unit is reserved before you arrive. Keep your transport booking separate from any vehicle reservation and read the written conditions before sending money.

references.label: DT Car · Used cars in Manila

title: Do accessories add to your used car's appraisal?
description: Document wheels, accessories and modifications so every purchase offer covers the same used car.
summary: List each modification, when it was fitted, who performed the work and whether the original part is included. An appraiser needs to know what will be on the car at handover.

sections.heading: Separate purchase cost from buyer value
paragraphs: New wheels or multimedia equipment may have cost the owner a substantial amount. That expense does not establish what another buyer will pay. Provide the receipt, photos and any installation paperwork. If you plan to remove an item, state that before an offer is made and show the replacement equipment.

sections.heading: Ask for an offer on one configuration
paragraphs: If the seller keeps a roof rack, for example, the buyer should know whether the mounting hardware stays and what the roof looks like after removal. Compare offers for the same configuration. Put the included accessories and spare parts on the handover inventory.

references.label: DT Car · Used cars in Manila

title: Used-car handover in Manila: keys, accessories and digital accounts
description: Use a handover inventory for spare keys, loose accessories and connected accounts when selling a car.
summary: Agree on a handover inventory before meeting. Count physical keys and remotes, confirm which accessories are included and arrange the transfer or removal of connected accounts through the manufacturer’s process.

sections.heading: Walk around the car with the inventory
paragraphs: Record the date and odometer, identify loose items such as a cargo cover, tools or charging cable, and have both parties note anything still due. If only one key is supplied, state that explicitly. A buyer who wants another key can request a separate replacement quote.

sections.heading: Protect saved information
paragraphs: Remove personal destinations and paired devices according to the vehicle manual. For a connected vehicle, ask the manufacturer how ownership is transferred and how the buyer confirms access. Avoid sharing your personal account password. Keep a copy of the signed inventory with the transaction records.

references.label: DT Car · Used cars in Manila

title: How to photograph scratches and dents for a car appraisal
description: Take appraisal photos that show both the location and detail of dents, scratches and previous repairs.
summary: Give the appraiser one photo showing where the mark is and a second showing its detail. A close-up with no surrounding panel is difficult to interpret.

sections.heading: Use a consistent sequence
paragraphs: Photograph the full side of the vehicle in daylight, then the affected door or bumper, then a close view from a slight angle. If a reflection hides the mark, move yourself or the car to change the angle. Keep the original files and do not digitally retouch the damage.

sections.heading: Label what you know
paragraphs: Write “left rear door, visible scratch” rather than guessing the repair cost. If a panel was repaired previously, say what was done and include any invoice you have. The buyer can use the images to prepare a preliminary range and confirm condition in person.

references.label: DT Car · Used cars in Manila

title: Bán xe ở Manila trước ngày về Việt Nam
description: Sắp xếp lịch xem xe và bàn giao tại Manila trước chuyến bay về Việt Nam, kèm mẫu hỏi giá thu mua.
summary: Chốt một ngày bàn giao bạn thực sự có mặt tại Manila. Tính ngược từ ngày đó để hẹn xem xe, thương lượng và xác nhận cách thanh toán, nhất là khi bạn vẫn cần xe đi làm tới sát ngày bay.

sections.heading: Nếu còn hai người mua đang hỏi
paragraphs: Gửi cho từng bên cùng một bộ ảnh, số km và thời điểm bạn có thể giao. Hỏi giá sau khi trừ phí, ai đến lấy xe và liệu có được kiểm tra tại nơi hẹn. Một lời trả giá cao nhưng chỉ hẹn sau ngày bay có thể không phù hợp với lịch của bạn.

sections.heading: Mẫu tin nhắn cho đội thu mua
paragraphs: “Mình bán [hãng, mẫu, bản, năm], đã đi [km], đang ở [khu vực]. Có thể xem xe [hai khung giờ], bàn giao chậm nhất [ngày]. Nhờ báo khoản thực nhận và những hồ sơ cần đối chiếu.” Nếu còn khoản vay, xin số tất toán từ bên cho vay. Nếu phải nhờ người khác bàn giao, xác nhận trước giấy tờ đối tác yêu cầu.

title: VinFast VF 9 Plus price in the Philippines: compare the two quotes
description: Compare Philippine VF 9 Plus starting prices and test the seating and luggage space before requesting a quote.
summary: The Philippine price list checked on 25 November 2026 shows the VF 9 Plus from ₱3,845,000 with battery subscription and ₱5,390,000 without subscription. The upfront difference is ₱1,545,000.

sections.heading: What does the difference buy?
paragraphs: Ask for two written quotations for the same VF 9 Plus. Put vehicle price, battery arrangement, recurring charges, insurance and any promotion on separate lines. A large upfront gap tells you how much cash differs at purchase. It does not tell you the lower-cost option over your ownership period.

sections.heading: What to confirm on a demonstration
paragraphs: If you carry passengers in every row, test access with the seating positions you actually use. Bring the dimensions of your largest case and measure cargo space with the seats occupied. Ask which variant and battery arrangement the dealer can supply and when the offer expires.

title: VinFast VF 6 Eco or Plus: how much is the upgrade?
description: Compare the VF 6 Eco and Plus upgrade cost under both Philippine battery arrangements.
summary: At the Philippine starting prices checked on 25 November 2026, the VF 6 Plus adds ₱160,000 over Eco with subscription, or ₱200,000 without subscription. Compare equipment at the same battery arrangement.

sections.heading: Read the four figures in pairs
paragraphs: With subscription, Eco starts at ₱1,249,000 and Plus at ₱1,409,000. Without subscription, the respective figures are ₱1,499,000 and ₱1,699,000. Comparing Plus with subscription against Eco without subscription mixes a trim decision with a recurring-cost decision.

sections.heading: Turn the upgrade into a test-drive question
paragraphs: List three items that matter on your commute and ask the adviser to show them on the exact Philippine variant. Common items to try include seat adjustment, parking visibility and the controls you use frequently. Get the two equipment sheets dated and save them alongside the offers before choosing.

title: VinFast VF 7 Eco versus Plus: Philippine price differences
description: Read all four Philippine VF 7 starting prices and compare Eco and Plus within the same battery arrangement.
summary: The price difference between VF 7 Eco and Plus depends on battery arrangement. The Philippine list checked on 25 November 2026 gives a ₱120,000 trim difference with subscription and ₱620,000 without subscription.

sections.heading: Why a single upgrade figure can mislead
paragraphs: With battery subscription, Eco starts at ₱1,430,000 and Plus at ₱1,550,000. Without subscription, Eco starts at ₱1,760,000 and Plus at ₱2,380,000. A dealer may quote a different payable amount after a promotion. Keep the list-price comparison and the dated actual offers on separate lines.

sections.heading: Choose the vehicle you can actually receive
paragraphs: Ask for the trim, model year, equipment, battery terms and delivery estimate together. If only one trim is on display, note which features you were able to test and which still need written confirmation. For financing, request comparable term lengths and deposits from the provider.

title: Reserving a VinFast in the Philippines: what to get in writing
description: Keep the vehicle configuration, payment reference and delivery conditions together when reserving a VinFast.
summary: Before paying, identify who receives the reservation, what unit it covers, and which event triggers the next payment. A configured online quote and a confirmed allocation are different stages.

sections.heading: Keep the configuration with the receipt
paragraphs: Write down model year, trim, colour and battery plan. VinFast’s Philippine reservation page allows configuration and shows estimated installment information. If a salesperson arranges the transaction, ask which entity issues the receipt and what reference you can use for follow-up.

sections.heading: If delivery timing matters
paragraphs: Give the latest date when delivery would still work for you. Ask whether the date in the quotation is an estimate, when the team will confirm allocation, and what options exist if the requested colour or trim is delayed. Obtain the current cancellation or refund terms before authorising payment.

title: Will a VinFast fit my parking space? A test-drive measurement guide
description: Measure a parking entrance, bay and door clearance before taking a VinFast test drive.
summary: Measure the route into the space as well as the bay itself. A car may fit on paper but leave insufficient room to turn in, open a door or reach a charging port.

sections.heading: Make a three-measurement sketch
paragraphs: Record the narrowest entrance width, usable bay length with the gate closed and clearance alongside the driver's door. Mark posts, ramps and walls rather than relying on the parking bay’s painted lines. If the space is shared, measure with the neighbouring vehicle in its usual position.

sections.heading: Use the demonstration safely
paragraphs: Bring the sketch and ask the adviser to show mirror position, charging port location and tailgate opening on the actual trim. Measure with permission while parked. If a home trial is unavailable, use the figures to identify which access point still needs a physical check before reservation.

title: Taking delivery of a VinFast EV: a first-day handover list
description: Check the order, keys, charging demonstration and outstanding items on VinFast delivery day.
summary: Before leaving, match the vehicle to the paperwork, inventory the items supplied and ask for a charging demonstration on your specific car. Keep one written record of any outstanding items.

sections.heading: Make a record while everyone is present
paragraphs: Check the variant, colour, vehicle identifier on the paperwork, odometer and the number of keys. Review the accessories included in your written order. Photograph any visible issue with the delivery team and agree who will follow up and by what date.

sections.heading: Make the first charge easier
paragraphs: Ask the team to demonstrate the charge-port release and how to see charging status using the manual for that model. Locate the support contact and ask where your warranty and service records are kept. If account activation is pending, ask for the reference number and a way to follow up after departure.

title: How much EV range do I need for a Manila commute?
description: Estimate the energy for a daily Manila commute using a round trip, detour and observed consumption.
summary: Start with the longest repeatable day between reliable charging opportunities. Include the return journey, errands and a detour allowance. Use observed energy consumption when you have it.

sections.heading: Build a realistic driving day
paragraphs: An illustrative 24 km trip each way, a 12 km school pickup and a 10 km detour make a 70 km day. At an assumed 17 kWh per 100 km, that day needs about 11.9 kWh of driving energy. This figure is a planning example, not a consumption rating for any VinFast model.

sections.heading: Test the assumptions
paragraphs: Log distance and energy for several typical days with air conditioning, usual passenger load and the routes you actually drive. Compare those results with how often you can charge. A brochure range measured under a test cycle cannot predict a specific congested day or access to a working charger.

title: How to check a V-Green charging bill in the Philippines
description: Check V-Green charging prices, promotion eligibility, session history and overstay charges in the Philippines.
summary: VinFast announced a phased introduction of payments at selected V-Green stations beginning 11 November 2026. Check the station and your vehicle’s eligibility in the VinFast app before assuming a session will be free or chargeable.

sections.heading: Before starting a session
paragraphs: Confirm the charger location, activated payment arrangements and the applicable price or privilege in your account. The manufacturer’s announcement distinguishes the rollout at individual stations from existing eligible free-charging privileges. Save the displayed terms if you need to reconcile a business trip later.

sections.heading: After unplugging
paragraphs: Open the session record and match its date, location and delivered energy to your visit. If the amount looks different from the expected charge, retain the session reference and contact the provider through its support channel. Do not send payment details in a public comment. The dated notice lists ₱17 per kWh for VinFast EVs where payment is active, before eligible promotions, and a separate DC overstay fee after a ten-minute grace period. Check current terms displayed for your session.

title: How long will an EV charging stop take on a Philippine trip?
description: Estimate charging time from the energy needed and average power, with room for traffic and queues.
summary: Estimate the energy you need to add and divide by the expected average charging power. Add time for access, queueing and starting the session. A station’s peak rating alone is insufficient.

sections.heading: Work through a stop
paragraphs: For an illustrative 24 kWh top-up, an average delivery rate of 30 kW implies 0.8 hours, or 48 minutes, of charging. At an average 20 kW, the same energy takes 72 minutes. Neither figure includes a queue. Actual power can change during a session and depends on the vehicle and charger.

sections.heading: Plan around your next appointment
paragraphs: Check connector compatibility, operating access and a backup site before departure. A stop chosen for a lunch break can be useful only if the charger is accessible at that time. After the trip, keep your actual session duration and delivered kWh to improve your next estimate.

title: EV charging site proposal: how to document the parking layout
description: Prepare a parking sketch and traffic-flow photos for a Philippine EV charging site survey.
summary: A useful parking plan shows how a vehicle enters, occupies a charging bay and leaves while the rest of the property remains accessible. Provide a sketch and photographs taken in the same direction.

sections.heading: Draw the busiest hour
paragraphs: Mark gates, entry controls, loading areas, existing parking and any access route that must stay open. Use arrows for normal traffic and note the time when deliveries or guest arrivals overlap. Add dimensions that someone can verify on site; label anything estimated.

sections.heading: Give the survey team a specific question
paragraphs: For example, a proposed bay near the entrance may be easy to find but may block a delivery vehicle when occupied. Photograph the normal delivery path and ask the survey team to compare an alternate bay. Final bay placement and electrical design depend on qualified site assessment.

references.label: DT Car · EV charging site proposals

title: Can a gated property host public EV charging?
description: Describe gated access, holiday hours and driver directions in an EV charging site proposal.
summary: Separate the hours vehicles can enter the property from the hours someone can resolve access problems. A station behind a gate can appear available to a driver while the site itself is closed.

sections.heading: Map the last arrival of the day
paragraphs: Write down when security closes the entrance, whether vehicles already inside may leave later, and how weekend or holiday hours differ. If charging would serve guests only, say so in the proposal. Describe any parking ticket or visitor registration step and who can authorise exceptions.

sections.heading: Test the access instructions
paragraphs: Ask a colleague unfamiliar with the site to follow the proposed entry directions during normal opening hours. Record confusing signs, blocked turns and the actual path from the street. Send those observations and the site contact to the operator for review before listing public availability.

references.label: DT Car · EV charging site proposals

title: Home or public charging: compare the cost of a mixed routine
description: Use a worked peso example to compare home and public charging in a monthly EV budget.
summary: Weight the two charging prices by the energy obtained at each location. Averaging prices without checking the share of energy can give the wrong monthly budget.

sections.heading: An example using 200 kWh
paragraphs: At illustrative rates of ₱12 and ₱22 per kWh, buying 150 kWh at home and 50 kWh publicly costs ₱2,900, or ₱14.50 per kWh. Splitting the same amount equally costs ₱3,400. The ₱500 difference comes from where the energy was purchased, even though the car drove the same route.

sections.heading: Replace the assumptions with receipts
paragraphs: Use billed kWh and the relevant tariff for each session. Track parking or session fees separately and then add them to your monthly total. If some charging is covered by an eligible privilege, record those sessions separately and model what the budget looks like if the privilege changes.

title: Fleet dashcam SIM installation: how to match devices to vehicles
description: Match dashcam devices, SIM references and test events to the correct fleet vehicle at installation.
summary: Give each installation a record connecting the vehicle, device and SIM inventory reference. Without that link a perfectly good SIM can appear missing when a vehicle or camera moves.

sections.heading: Prepare the batch before opening vehicles
paragraphs: Have dispatch provide a dated vehicle roster and identify vehicles unavailable that day. Assign one row per unit. Keep full SIM identifiers and platform credentials in the operator's authorised system. Use a short reference on circulated progress sheets so a supervisor can reconcile records without distributing sensitive account details.

sections.heading: Close the row with an observed result
paragraphs: Log who fitted the SIM, which vehicle was present and whether the platform received the expected test event. If a unit does not report, record the time and symptom rather than marking it complete. Agree who owns the next check before the vehicle returns to service.

title: Testing fleet dashcam footage at night before acceptance
description: Define a night-time dashcam footage test and document what the fleet reviewer accepted.
summary: Define what the fleet needs to see in its normal operating conditions. A daytime image in the depot will not answer whether glare obscures a night pickup.

sections.heading: Specify a repeatable sample
paragraphs: With operator permission, choose a controlled route or parked test position with representative lighting. Record time, camera position and any lighting changes. Have an authorised reviewer check the original footage rather than a compressed screenshot shared in a chat. Keep identifiable passengers out of demonstrations unless appropriate permissions are in place.

sections.heading: Record a decision that can be reproduced
paragraphs: If reflections obscure a required area, describe where and under which lighting. Have the installer review the fit and repeat the same sample. Record the approved clip reference, reviewer and time. Restrict access to the test media using the fleet's normal controls.

title: Planning taxi meter installation across an active Philippine fleet
description: Plan meter installation slots, release checks and missed appointments across a working taxi depot.
summary: Schedule vehicles by actual depot availability and reserve separate time for functional checks. Installation completion and authorisation to place a meter into commercial use are distinct items to confirm with the operator.

sections.heading: Use a small first batch
paragraphs: Start with a representative vehicle and the agreed device model. Measure access time, installation time, checking time and return-to-dispatch time separately. For example, a 30-minute installation plus 15 minutes of queueing and checks occupies a 45-minute slot before any rework.

sections.heading: Tell dispatch how to handle exceptions
paragraphs: Agree who can release the vehicle, what evidence is required and which operator or authority confirms any calibration or compliance step. If a vehicle misses its slot, assign the next ready unit rather than leaving an installation team waiting. Keep a dated exception list for the next shift.

title: How to manage rework after a fleet installation batch
description: Track vehicle installation exceptions from original job reference through retest and release.
summary: Track exceptions by vehicle and issue. A total such as “six units pending” does not tell dispatch which vehicles can work or what the installer must bring back.

sections.heading: Separate the failure modes
paragraphs: Give each exception a plain description, such as missing evidence, device offline or inaccessible vehicle. Include the original job reference, test time, responsible party and next booking. Store images in the authorised project folder and share a reference in the log.

sections.heading: Close only after the agreed retest
paragraphs: If a camera reported offline during handover, a photo showing the camera mounted does not close the connectivity issue. Record a successful platform check or the operator's agreed acceptance evidence. Keep initial and final results so the next batch benefits from the pattern.

title: How many spare EVs should a fleet pilot budget for?
description: Estimate spare EV requirements from peak dispatch demand, charging conflicts and service downtime.
summary: Count how many vehicles dispatch needs simultaneously, then model charging, maintenance and unplanned downtime at the busiest point of the day. A percentage based on total fleet size can hide a peak-hour shortage.

sections.heading: Build one peak-hour example
paragraphs: Suppose dispatch needs eight active vehicles at 17:00. Of ten available units, one is charging and one is due for service. That leaves eight ready and no margin for a late return. If an extra unit is delayed, only seven can start. These are planning assumptions, not a recommended fleet ratio.

sections.heading: Try scheduling changes before increasing orders
paragraphs: Move one planned activity to a quieter hour if operations allow and repeat the calculation. Compare the cost of one spare with the cost and feasibility of changing the charging schedule. Give procurement the peak shortfall and the assumptions behind it before requesting a quote.

title: What should a Philippine EV fleet driver record on a pilot shift?
description: Capture distance, charging time and exceptions in a driver shift log for a Philippine fleet pilot.
summary: A short shift log should explain lost time and energy use without distracting the driver. Collect readings while parked at handover and at planned stops.

sections.heading: Use five fields the driver can finish
paragraphs: Record shift identifier, odometer at start and finish, charge percentage at the handovers, charging session references and unusual delays. Keep passenger names and exact personal trip details out of the pilot summary. Have dispatch attach route and vehicle references from its own records.

sections.heading: Read the log with dispatch
paragraphs: Two vehicles can cover the same distance yet spend different time queueing to charge. Separate the wait for a bay from time drawing energy. If a vehicle returned late, distinguish passenger demand, traffic, charger access and maintenance. Use the pilot data to adjust one variable before the next trial.

title: An EV warning appeared: what to record for your service adviser
description: Record a dashboard warning and contact an adviser with the exact wording, time and circumstances.
summary: When safely parked, record the exact warning and the circumstances in which it appeared. Follow the vehicle manual and the manufacturer’s assistance instructions for any warning about stopping or continuing.

sections.heading: Describe the sequence in ordinary language
paragraphs: A message such as “After a public charging session, the display showed [exact words] before I selected drive” is more useful than guessing which part failed. Note time, mileage and whether the warning was still present when parked. Take a photo only when safe. Do not recreate a fault on the road to obtain evidence.

sections.heading: Ask what happens before the appointment
paragraphs: Give the adviser the model and current vehicle location. Ask whether the vehicle should stay parked and whether assistance or collection is appropriate. Wait for model-specific guidance before moving it if safe operation is in doubt. Request a reference number so the workshop can find the initial report.

title: Organising VinFast service records before resale in the Philippines
description: Organise VinFast maintenance records, open work and coverage enquiries before a vehicle sale.
summary: Put the maintenance history in date and mileage order, then identify open items. A buyer should be able to distinguish completed work from a recommendation or an unapproved estimate.

sections.heading: Build a one-page index
paragraphs: Use the visit date, odometer, job order reference, work completed and any next action. Keep the original paperwork. If a visit involved a software update or recurring issue, record the description from the workshop rather than interpreting the technical cause. Redact personal contact information in copies used for initial enquiries.

sections.heading: Ask about coverage before making promises
paragraphs: For a buyer asking about remaining coverage, request confirmation from the appropriate service provider using the vehicle details through its private channel. Warranty conditions can depend on the actual policy and history. Share the dated response and distinguish vehicle coverage from accessories or a separate service agreement.

title: When an EV issue returns after a workshop visit
description: Prepare a timeline and job-order reference when an EV symptom returns after a workshop visit.
summary: Link the repeat visit to the first job order. A clear before-and-after timeline helps the workshop see whether the original symptom returned or a different issue has appeared.

sections.heading: Write a short timeline
paragraphs: For example, note “warning reported Monday at 12,300 km, vehicle collected Wednesday, same wording appeared Friday at 12,410 km.” Add the work listed on the first job order and the conditions of the second occurrence. Avoid assigning blame or replacing parts based on a guess.

sections.heading: Agree the next contact point
paragraphs: Ask who is reviewing the first visit, what additional diagnostic work needs approval and when you should expect an update. If the vehicle might be unsafe to operate, follow manufacturer instructions and ask about assistance before driving to the workshop. At collection, request the findings and any remaining monitoring instructions in writing.

title: Green GSM driver interview in the Philippines: how to prepare
description: Prepare a driving example and confirm the depot, document list and assessment schedule for Green GSM.
summary: Prepare a concise driving history and ask recruitment to confirm the current interview location, time and document list. Green GSM’s published process includes an in-person interview and driving assessment.

sections.heading: Practise describing one actual shift
paragraphs: Choose a route you know and explain how you handled a changed pickup point or a passenger who needed clearer directions. Give a concrete example of your customer service and local route knowledge. If your experience comes from delivery or company driving, say so accurately and explain what transfers to passenger service.

sections.heading: Before leaving home
paragraphs: Check the latest official visit instructions, your licence validity and the contact for a schedule change. Ask whether the driving assessment will take place on the same day. Save the confirmation so you can show the details at the correct entrance. If you miss the appointment, request a new slot through the same channel.

title: Green GSM driver income: questions to ask about a Philippine offer
description: Compare guaranteed and variable components of a driver offer and confirm the terms for your depot.
summary: Green GSM advertises potential income on its recruitment page. Ask the recruiter for the breakdown that applies to your particular arrangement, depot and shift before treating any advertised maximum as a personal budget.

sections.heading: Separate each component
paragraphs: Request the guaranteed amount, if any, the variable components, eligibility conditions and payment frequency in writing. Ask for one illustrative ordinary week and what changes if a shift is missed. If an incentive is mentioned, check whether it is a one-off or recurring payment and who verifies qualification.

sections.heading: Compare work arrangements consistently
paragraphs: Someone applying to drive a company taxi and someone renting an EV may face different expenses and obligations. Write down who provides the vehicle, who pays charging costs and which party handles downtime. Ask Green GSM to confirm the final offer and save its date before comparing it with another opportunity.

title: Paano ihanda ang litrato ng parking para sa EV rental?
description: Ihanda ang larawan ng parking slot at pasukan, at kumpirmahin kung saan ito ipapasa para sa EV rental.
summary: Bago magpadala ng litrato, itanong sa rental team kung anong detalye ang kailangan para sa kasalukuyang application. Ipakita ang aktuwal na puwesto at ang daan papasok nang malinaw.

sections.heading: Kunan ang puwesto sa normal na gamit nito
paragraphs: Magkuha ng isang malawak na larawan mula sa pasukan at isa pang kita ang buong parking slot. Kung may gate o poste, ipakita kung saan lulusot ang sasakyan. Huwag isama ang mukha ng kapitbahay, ID o dokumentong hindi kailangan sa application. Kung shared ang garahe, sabihin kung kailan mo ito magagamit.

sections.heading: Kung inuupahan mo ang parking
paragraphs: Itanong kung kailangan ng team ang pahintulot ng may-ari o property manager at saang opisyal na channel ito dapat isumite. Ang pagkakaroon ng parking slot ay hiwalay sa pahintulot na maglagay ng charger. Hintayin ang kumpirmasyon ng rental team bago ituring na aprubado ang puwesto.
